earnings.title: PACKAGING CORPORATION OF AMERICA REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS
highlights: Lake Forest, IL, October 21, 2026 – Packaging Corporation of America (NYSE: PKG) today reported third quarter 2026 net income of $262 million, or $2.93 per share, and net income of $272 million, or $3.04 per share, excluding special items.
Third quarter net sales were $2.6 billion in 2026 and $2.3 billion in 2025.
In the Paper segment, sales volume was down 2.5% from the third quarter of 2025.

quotes.text: We executed very well across all aspects of our operations, resulting in very strong earnings performance for the quarter despite continued cost headwinds from freight, recycled fiber and chemicals and some weakness in agricultural end markets in our corrugated business.

items.heading: General Economic Conditions – A deterioration in general economic conditions may harm our business, results of operations, cash flows, and financial position.
items.group: Risks Related to our Operations, Business and Industry

items.heading: Industry Cyclicality – Changes in the prices of our products could materially affect our financial condition, results of operations, and liquidity.
items.group: Risks Related to our Operations, Business and Industry

items.heading: Competition – The intensity of competition in the industries in which we operate could result in downward pressure on pricing and volume, which could lower earnings and operating cash flows.
items.group: Risks Related to our Operations, Business and Industry

items.heading: Cost of Fiber – An increase in the cost of fiber could increase our manufacturing costs and lower our earnings.
items.group: Risks Related to our Operations, Business and Industry

items.heading: Cost of Purchased Fuels and Chemicals – An increase in the cost of purchased fuels and chemicals could lead to higher manufacturing costs, resulting in reduced earnings.
items.group: Risks Related to our Operations, Business and Industry

items.heading: Transportation Costs – Reduced truck and rail availability could lead to higher costs or poorer service, resulting in lower earnings, and harm our ability to distribute our products.
